approves.text:
The Project Owner approves the 20 decisions below, each as written in docs/DECISION_ISSUE_IDEA_IMPLEMENTATION_REGISTER_v0.1.md at commit 24423eb593b213c46bbb71bd82b60b585793b079. Each row is copied verbatim from the register.

| DEC-034 | **AI disclosure policy for the submission** (proposed by PM, owner approval required): (1) the *Use of Artificial Intelligence* field lists every AI system and exactly what it did, including what it got wrong (e.g. RES-009) — the verification loop is part of the method, not hidden; (2) AAL is named as the multi-agent orchestration platform developed by CCTI (private), with the roles it assigned; (3) metadata: commit trailers from now on, an `AI_USE` section in the README covering the earlier history, and the ledger (every external analysis entry names its model); (4) every image/video produced by AI or AI-written code carries a visible label; no NASA branding in generated material; (5) analysis methods are declared with their maturity level (V/P/D, DEC-014) — capability claims are limited to what the evidence shows | Proposed |

| DEC-041 | **Analysis record: `docs/analysis/AR-001_B6_spread_rate_window_correction.md` (ledger seq 103).** **B6 headline result corrected (owner approval 2026-11-10, after RES-022):** "B6, BASS-II 100 µm PMMA, AIR display 3 interval (18.5–28.6 s): leading-edge spread rate ≈ 2.0 mm/s — 1.99 mm/s (reference: 0.1 of frame peak), statistical 95 % 1.84–2.13, front-definition range 1.99–2.20 (relative) / up to 2.54 (absolute), rule variants 1.88–2.07, scale ±3 %, ruler–sample parallax and luminous-edge–pyrolysis offset [UNKNOWN]; AIR display to cm/s mapping open (ISS-013)." RES-001 (2.274 ± 0.094 mm/s, 13–53 s chosen by hand, iid fit SE) is kept as history and superseded as headline (ledger supersession). Consequences: (a) RES-002 family values (B6 2.32 ± 0.10, B15 2.39 ± 0.10) were measured with the pre-R-W windows and iid SE; they are qualified as superseded method, to be re-measured under R-W when each run's overlay is transcribed; (b) RES-002's observation "B6 ≈ B15 despite higher B15 flow" is **withdrawn** — it compared flow-mixed B6 with B15; (c) release acceptance (RELEASE_A: "B6 reproduced against published ≈2 mm/s within declared uncertainty") is assessed only after the comparator's own conditions are matched — agreement is not a reason for the choice (DEC-032 note stands) | Approved (owner) |

| DEC-056 | **(PM, under the owner's 2026-11-11 mandate to decide while he is away.)** No change to R-W3 (frozen during the test; a change chosen after seeing the truth would be fitted to it). Instead, every GFL spread rate is reported as a **luminous-edge rate**, with the interval labelled "statistical + threshold-definition systematic; excludes any change in the offset between the luminous edge and the pyrolysis front (unknown; in the synthetic tests it reached +5 % in T4 and, undeclared, +1.8 % in T1)". The jury text and the dashboard carry this wording. Calibration for later: an explicit offset term requires a front measurement independent of luminosity (thermocouple or surface-temperature data), which GFL has not located in PSI-25 for these runs (not yet searched systematically) | Decided (PM); owner review 12 Nov |

| DEC-057 | **(PM.) Window rule R-W4 declared** (`docs/WINDOW_RULE_R-W4.md`, `tools/window_rule_r4.py`, tests `tests/test_window_rule_r4.py`; sealed seq 197–199 and anchored before any real run): the burn record starts at the first frame passing G1 **and** G2 (ISS-049); everything else is R-W3. B11 results under R-W4 are post-protocol, reported separately and never counted as supported predictions. Adoption as the release rule: owner's decision | Declared (PM); owner review 12 Nov |

| DEC-058 | **(Owner, 2026-11-11 21:35.) All results obtained before the official challenge resources are published stay "open"** and are compared with the results on NASA's official data. The comparison is pre-registered in `docs/OFFICIAL_DATA_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL_v1.md` before the official data exist: SHA-256 identity check first; identical bytes confirm the open results unchanged; different bytes mean a re-run with frozen rules and both results reported side by side | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-059 | **(Owner, 2026-11-11 22:54.) Chemical kinetics are a deliberate limit of GFL, documented as such.** In the thermal regime of opposed-flow thin-fuel spread the rate is set by heat transfer, not by reaction rate (de Ris 1969; Bhattacharjee et al. 2016); chemistry matters near the kinetic (blow-off) and radiative (low-flow quench) limits. GFL's role is to state which regime a run is in (CRAM-2), not to model kinetics. Written in `docs/METHODS_AND_VALIDATION_v1.md` §1.1 and kept for the jury Q&A ("why is there no chemistry?") | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-060 | **(Owner, 2026-11-11 23:48.) The analysis modules become platform code now, before the official data arrive; every module and every research direction is visible on the platform with its maturity.** Built as `src/gfl_analysis` (A0–A7), data-agnostic: the modules run on the four measured runs now and on the official challenge files when they arrive (DEC-058). Frozen rule code stays in `tools/` as sealed; the platform imports it. Research directions that disappeared without a decision (dynamic dependency analysis, state estimation, physical model and parameter registry; audit finding on dossier docs 21–22) are restored as documented directions | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-061 | **(Owner, 2026-11-12 00:37.) Predictions become a user function, "pre-registered test" (`src/gfl_analysis/predict.py`, CLI `propose` / `score`).** A physicist names a target run and a measured reference; GFL proposes the expected rate from a stated law (thin-fuel 1/thickness, or the empirical exponent measured so far) with a band, or takes the user's own; the prediction is sealed before the target is opened; scoring uses the frozen rule and includes the reference run's uncertainty; out-of-domain targets get no proposal, with the reason; not testable never counts as supported | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-062 | **(PM proposal 2026-11-12 03:01, owner "ok" 03:17.) Data storage.** The source of truth for NASA files is the NASA PSI archive plus the SHA-256 fingerprints in the ledger: anyone can re-download and check (done once already, RES-003). Raw NASA bytes do not go into Git and not into Git LFS. A private Azure Blob container may hold a backup copy for the team; no server is needed. GFL's own derived data stay in the repository. Copyrighted papers are cited and linked, never redistributed | Decided (owner signature pending) |

| DEC-063 | **(Owner, 2026-11-12 03:01, proposals by Cristina.)** (a) an interactive architecture map from each function to its code, with icons and a measure of usability; (b) a file explorer; (c) for non-IT users: how to import data and analyses from other sources and in what format, how to export, how to generate a report | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-064 | **(Owner's opinion 2026-11-12 13:33, PM decides.) The database described in dossier document 6 is not rebuilt.** It was never built in this repository; GFL states it as not built and unusable. Reason: its contents would be replaced by the official challenge data, which become GFL's time-zero reference (T0), and the other sources are already sealed in the ledger. Consequence checked: no result, chart or module reads from it, so nothing else changes. **Also decided by the owner:** the P2 modules are built now, not after the official data arrive; when the data come, GFL is populated and tested, and functions are reopened only if they fail | Decided (owner signature pending) |

| DEC-065 | **(Owner, 2026-11-12 13:39.) P2 is done before the official data arrive, not after.** Every module is made functional now; when the NASA data arrive GFL is only populated, tested and analysed, and a function is reopened only if it fails. P2: dim-flame front at 17 % O₂ (ISS-029), rebuild of every result with one command, and the PSI-25 integrity audit (DEC-022) | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-066 | **(Owner, 2026-11-12 14:57; protocol by PM.) Independent evaluation of GFL after P2** (`docs/GFL_EVALUATION_PROTOCOL_v1.md`, registered and anchored before any evaluator runs). Three models from three providers, one role each, one call, no history: juror grok-4.7, physicist gpt-6-astra, user Kimi-K2.6. They receive one packet copied from the repository (`tools/build_evaluation_packet.py`), not the code, the raw files or the page. Every statement needs a file and a verbatim quote; a deterministic scorer (`tools/score_evaluation.py`) counts only statements whose quote is in the packet, and marks three reading checks, one of which asks about a section that does not exist. The PM built GFL and does not evaluate it; the PM classes the verified weaknesses against the repository and publishes the classing. The decision on run B16 (new rule R-W5 or not) waits for the evaluators' answer to question G2 | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-067 | **(Owner, 2026-11-13.) One release result for B6: rule R-W4.** 2.20 mm/s, reported interval 1.91–2.37 mm/s, luminous-edge rate, shown on the first page, in the README, the methods document and the reports. 1.99 mm/s (R-W2, front at 0.1 of peak) and 2.274 mm/s (hand window, RES-001) stay as history. All four evaluators of DEC-066 recommended a single headline under R-W4. Run B16 stays not measurable under the frozen rule; no rule R-W5 is written (specified, not built) | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-068 | **(Owner, 2026-11-13.) The provisional status of DEC-058 is lifted.** The Resources tab of the challenge names the NASA PSI Data Repository as its data source; there is no separate official package. GFL's BASS-II files are from that source, so results are no longer labelled open until compared with official data. They remain luminous-edge rates from one flight per condition | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-069 | **(Owner, 2026-11-13.) Verification policy: zero trust, not human authority.** GFL's results are checked by independent models in separate roles and by re-execution. The absence of a human combustion reviewer is not presented as a weakness on the page, in the history or in the reports; one factual sentence stays in the methods document and the AI disclosure. What nobody can settle from NASA's public archive (pyrolysis front, flow at the sample, replicate runs) is stated as limits of the evidence and as the next research question | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-070 | **(Owner, 2026-11-13.) Honest labels (package B).** Regime shown as "consistent with"; the theory range named a sensitivity range with its construction; prediction ratio intervals include the reference run's interval; the observable-equivalence gate says it checks the procedure; boundary conditions are partial because mounting, pressure history and flow at the sample are not recorded; B13's flickering air display makes its flow gate partial. Internal regime keys are unchanged | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-071 | **(Owner, 2026-11-13.) Fire-safety evidence map across the 24 PSI combustion investigations (package C).** Extraction of NASA's own record text by two Foundry models (grok-4.7, Kimi-K2.6) run on the owner's machine, every extracted statement with a verbatim quote, checked by a deterministic validator; protocol and schema sealed before the run; GFL's transfer gates applied between investigations. Planned functions (enriched oxygen, partial gravity, Earth applications) are shown as specified, not built | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-072 | **(Owner, 2026-11-14.) Browser title and authorship tag.** Title "GFL | Microgravity Combustion Analysis Platform"; the tag reads "Human + AI, checked by re-execution", top right, with the AI-generated logo and icons stated in the footer | Decided (owner) |

| DEC-073 | **(PM proposal, 2026-11-14; owner asked for more data and analyses and left the plan to the PM.) Saffire measured from NASA's images under a rule frozen first.** Rule R-S1 (`docs/SAFFIRE_RULE_R-S1.md`) is written and anchored before any Saffire flame image is opened. It is accepted only if it reproduces both rates NASA reports for the Saffire-II SIBAL strips within 20 %; otherwise the failure is reported and Saffire-I is not measured with it. The third extractor is kept: replacing it after seeing its answers would choose the result; disputes are shown beside NASA's run tables instead (A6) | Proposed; owner signature pending |

Order of precedence. Where a later decision in this batch changes an earlier one, the later one applies and the earlier text stands as history: DEC-067 replaces the B6 headline of DEC-041 (1.99 mm/s under R-W2 becomes history; 2.20 mm/s under R-W4 is the release result) and settles the adoption left open in DEC-057 and the B16 question DEC-066 left waiting; DEC-068 lifts the provisional status of DEC-058, so the references to separate official challenge data in DEC-060, DEC-064 and DEC-065 read as the NASA PSI Data Repository; DEC-073 extends the extraction of DEC-071 from two models to three, the third being kept.
